coverageNotes: Tests the parent/component rollback boundary and awaiting the actual call. Uses the original unchanged local component pinned to 1.41.0. Does not assess authoring or mounting a component.

questions.concept: A caught component mutation error rolls back its subtransaction while its caller may commit
questions.context:
Convex 1.41.0. A mounted auditSink component owns audits { event: string }. Its mutation components.auditSink.index.writeAudit accepts { event: string, failAfterWrite: boolean }, inserts an audit row, then throws if failAfterWrite is true.

The root schema has auditStatuses { event: string, status: "audit_succeeded" | "audit_failed" }. A root mutation has validated args { event: string, shouldFail: boolean }. ctx, args, and components are in scope. Each option is the complete root handler body.
questions.question: Which handler commits the matching status and returns it normally in both cases, with a successful audit kept and a failed audit insert rolled back?

options.rationale: Rethrowing aborts the root transaction too. Its audit_failed insert is rolled back and the caller receives an error.
runQuery cannot execute a mutation reference. The actual call fails even when shouldFail is false, so a successful audit is incorrectly recorded as failed.
Awaiting runAfter waits for scheduling, not for the scheduled mutation to execute. A later audit error is not caught by this handler, which records audit_succeeded.
Awaiting runMutation observes the component outcome. Catching the error leaves the component insert rolled back while allowing the parent status write to commit.
